messages.author: 38226bd700051927
messages.subject: Re: CFA with ipsative data
parts:
It will depend on the type of data, most likely.

For questionnaire data, check out this:

https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-012-0217-x

The syntax shouldn't be difficult to adapt to lavaan IMO. If you allow me some self promotion as well, here I propose a MCMC Bayesian algorithm to estimate a model with forced-choice item pairs:

https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0146621616662226

However, it turns out to be (empirically) equivalent to Anna Brown's Thurstonian IRT for item pairs, which is more flexible as it allows for groups of more than 2 items (under certain assumptions of course).

If your data is not questionnaire responses, but something else, maybe check first how it turns out to be ipsative and whether it is necessary at all.
